title: Bounded finite conjunctive rule induction over typed N-ary facts

independentExamples.description: Two renamed positive entity graphs share a root-to-member edge and one member property while a negative graph changes only the property value.
independentExamples.expectedBehavior: Return the two-literal shared-variable conjunction with positive bindings and an exhaustive negative rejection.

independentExamples.description: A disconnected lookalike contains the same edge and property on different entities.
independentExamples.expectedBehavior: Reject it because one rule variable must bind the same entity in both literals.

preconditions: both positive and negative examples are present
the target root occurs in accepted evidence for every example
entity and value term kinds are declared before induction
facts, arity, variables, literals, candidates, and match steps remain bounded
invariants: the head variable is bound by a connected body
all rule constants come from typed value terms in visible positive evidence
a solved rule covers every positive and rejects every negative example
predicate names, values, entity names, fact order, and example order are data rather than control flow
candidate selection is shortest-body first with canonical variable and literal ordering
uncertaintySemantics: UNPARSED denotes malformed typed evidence. UNKNOWN denotes that no separator exists in the completely explored declared hypothesis space. RESOURCE_LIMIT denotes an exhausted example, fact, arity, variable, body, candidate, or match-search bound.
proofBehavior: Each positive receipt records the root-preserving variable binding and one supporting fact per body literal. Each negative receipt records completion of bounded match search. Verification reruns canonical induction, replays all joins, and compares the complete rule and evidence.
kbMigration: none; existing KB packages, rules, and reasoning methods are unchanged

guardianControls.fullRename: target, entity, predicate, value, example, and fact identifiers are all replaced
guardianControls.ordering: fact arrays and example arrays are reversed
guardianControls.contrast: a lookalike places the required property on a disconnected entity
guardianControls.nonIdentifiability: isomorphic positive and negative graphs return UNKNOWN
guardianControls.witnessTamper: a nonexistent support fact invalidates verification

proposedDescriptor.soundness: every solved rule covers all positive and rejects all negative examples under finite conjunctive-query semantics
proposedDescriptor.completeness: complete for connected positive conjunctive rules within the declared variable, literal, candidate, and match bounds

remainingGap: No official test or recursive-target claim is made. The reviewed method is registered and the complete validation split reproduces 126 solved, 10 unknown, and 64 resource-limited results through the public engine route. Quantification, negation, aggregation, arithmetic, and larger conjunctive search require later generic iterations.
